script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

A bustling coffee shop filled with customers. JAMES (40s), a quiet man with a well-groomed beard and glasses, sits alone at a corner table.

JAMES: (murmurs to himself) It's been ten years.

Waitress brings him a coffee.

WAITRESS: (smiling) Same as last time?

JAMES: (nods) Yes, thank you.

---

INT. CLASSROOM - NIGHT

James teaches a literature class at a community college. Students file in, some chatting quietly, others texting on their phones.

JAMES: (to the class) Good afternoon, class. Today, we'll be discussing "The Great Gatsby" by F. Scott Fitzgerald.

---

EXT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

After class, James takes a long walk outside. He sees EVELYN (30s), a former student, sitting on a bench.

EVELYN: (surprised) Professor James? I didn't know you took night walks.

JAMES: (smiling) I do from time to time.

They strike up a conversation.

---

INT. EVELYN'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Evelyn invites James to her apartment for dinner. They eat spaghetti and discuss their pasts.

EVELYN: (tearfully) I've always regretted the way things ended between us.

JAMES: (reassuringly) We all make mistakes, Evelyn. It's important to learn from them.

---

EXT. PARK - DAY

James and Evelyn sit on a bench, feeding ducks.

EVELYN: (softly) I've missed this, James. The quiet moments, the simplicity.

JAMES: (looking at her) And I've missed you, Evelyn.

---

INT. EVELYN'S KITCHEN - NIGHT

They cook dinner together, laughing and sharing stories.

---

EXT. STREET - NIGHT

Under the moonlit sky, James holds Evelyn's hand.

EVELYN: (wistfully) I can't believe this is happening.

JAMES: (smiling) Believe it, Evelyn. We both deserve a second chance.

---

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Ten years later, James and Evelyn sit in the same corner of the coffee shop.

EVELYN: (gazing at James) I've never been happier.

JAMES: (looking at her with love) And I, Evelyn, have never been more grateful.

---

FADE OUT.
